title: A map of finite modules that is split injective modulo arbitrarily high powers of a radical ideal is split injective
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $J\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (the intersection of all maximal ideals), and $u:N\to M$ a homomorphism of finitely generated $A$-modules. Suppose that for arbitrarily large integers $k$ the induced map $u_k:N/J^kN\to M/J^kM$ is a split injection, i.e. there is an $A$-linear $v_k:M/J^kM\to N/J^kN$ with $v_k\circ u_k=\mathrm{id}$. Then $u$ is a split injection: there is an $A$-linear $v:M\to N$ with $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion, line 18142), Section 'An application of Ext groups'

proof.text: *$u$ is injective.* Let $x\in\ker u$ and let $k$ be one of the integers for which $u_k$ has a left inverse $v_k$. The class $\bar x\in N/J^kN$ satisfies $u_k(\bar x)=\overline{u(x)}=0$, so $\bar x=v_k(u_k(\bar x))=0$, i.e. $x\in J^kN$. Since these $k$ are arbitrarily large and $J^kN\supseteq J^{k'}N$ for $k\le k'$, $x\in J^kN$ for every $k\ge0$, so $x\in\bigcap_kJ^kN=0$ by Krull's intersection theorem [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] applied to the Noetherian ring $A$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $J$ in the Jacobson radical and the finitely generated module $N$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion), lines 18148-18151 (Ker(phi) in I^nN for arbitrarily large n, then Lemma 00IQ)

proof.text: *A finite free presentation of the cokernel.* Put $Q=M/u(N)$ with projection $p:M\to Q$, so $0\to N\xrightarrow{u}M\xrightarrow{p}Q\to0$ is exact (step 1). $Q$ is finitely generated (images of generators of $M$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], so there is a surjection $\pi:F_0=A^a\to Q$ sending the basis to generators. Its kernel is a submodule of the finitely generated module $A^a$ over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence finitely generated [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]; choose a surjection $F_1=A^b\to\ker\pi$ and let $d_1:F_1\to F_0$ be its composite with the inclusion, so $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ is exact. (Stacks takes a resolution $F_2\to F_1\to F_0\to Q\to 0$; $F_2$ only serves to name the class of $\beta$ in $\mathrm{Ext}^1_A(Q,N)$ and is not needed for the argument.) Since $F_0$ is free and $p$ surjective, choose $\alpha:F_0\to M$ with $p\circ\alpha=\pi$ (send each basis vector to a preimage of its image). Then $p\circ\alpha\circ d_1=\pi\circ d_1=0$, so $\alpha\circ d_1$ takes values in $u(N)$, and since $u$ is injective there is a unique $A$-linear $\beta:F_1\to N$ with $u\circ\beta=\alpha\circ d_1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion), lines 18151-18162

proof.text: *Reduction modulo $J^k$.* Let $k$ be one of the integers of the hypothesis, $v_k:M/J^kM\to N/J^kN$ with $v_k\circ u_k=\mathrm{id}$, and $q_N:N\to N/J^kN$, $q_M:M\to M/J^kM$ the projections, so $u_k\circ q_N=q_M\circ u$. Put $\bar\gamma_k=v_k\circ q_M\circ\alpha:F_0\to N/J^kN$. Then $\bar\gamma_k\circ d_1=v_k\circ q_M\circ u\circ\beta=v_k\circ u_k\circ q_N\circ\beta=q_N\circ\beta$. Since $F_0$ is free and $q_N$ surjective, lift $\bar\gamma_k$ to an $A$-linear $\gamma_k:F_0\to N$ with $q_N\circ\gamma_k=\bar\gamma_k$; then $q_N\circ(\beta-\gamma_k\circ d_1)=0$, i.e. $\beta-\gamma_k\circ d_1$ maps $F_1$ into $J^kN$. (This is Stacks' 'arguing as above' for the reduced sequence, which is the 'only if' direction of the splitting criterion; written directly it needs neither the exactness of the reduced sequences nor of the reduced presentation.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion), lines 18166-18190

proof.text: *Translation into $\mathrm{Hom}$.* Let $H=\mathrm{Hom}_A(F_1,N)$ and $d_1^*:\mathrm{Hom}_A(F_0,N)\to H$, $\gamma\mapsto\gamma\circ d_1$. With the basis $e_1,\dots,e_b$ of $F_1=A^b$, $H\cong N^b$ via $f\mapsto(f(e_j))_j$, and $f$ maps $F_1$ into $J^kN$ iff each $f(e_j)\in J^kN$, iff $f\in J^kH$ (as $J^k(N^b)=(J^kN)^b$). So step 3 gives $\beta\in\mathrm{im}(d_1^*)+J^kH$ for arbitrarily large $k$. Let $C=H/\mathrm{im}(d_1^*)$ and $c$ the image of $\beta$ in $C$; then $c\in J^kC$ for arbitrarily large $k$, hence for all $k$ (the $J^kC$ decrease). $C$ is a quotient of $H\cong N^b$, a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], so $\bigcap_kJ^kC=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] ($A$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $J$ in the Jacobson radical). Hence $c=0$: there is $\gamma:F_0\to N$ with $\beta=\gamma\circ d_1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion), lines 18186-18202 (Lemma 00IQ applied to the cokernel of Hom(F_0,N) -> Hom(F_1,N))

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1 and 2, $u$ is injective, $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ is exact with $F_0$ free, $p\circ\alpha=\pi$ and $u\circ\beta=\alpha\circ d_1$; by step 4, $\beta=\gamma\circ d_1$ for some $\gamma:F_0\to N$. The splitting criterion [lem-weil-pbc-split-extension-free-presentation] gives an $A$-linear $v:M\to N$ with $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$, i.e. $u$ is a split injection.
